    spec multiaxis_control: Shared sin/cos unit for a 16-axis motor-control loop: a 1 MHz control tick issues 32 requests at once (Park + inverse Park per axis); all 32 results must be back within 0.44 us of the tick (p99 over ticks). Max error <= 2^-12. Minimise LUTs + FFs.
      constraint: throughput_msps >= 32
      constraint: max_abs_err <= 0.000244141
      constraint: sys_p99_batch_us <= 0.44
      objective: min luts_plus_ffs (HV ref 4000)
      objective: max accuracy_bits (HV ref 12)
      select: min luts_plus_ffs
      system (simulated at L2 for the shortlist; screened at L1 by an analytic bound): control loop: a tick every 1 us issues 32 requests at once (32 requests/us on average)
      budget: 400 evals, 100/round, <= 4 rounds, eps 0.01

args.notes: Spec: 32 requests per 1us tick, all 32 results back within 0.44us (p99), err <= 2^-12, min LUTs+FFs. Memory: pipelined_m m=4 (data_width=15, n_iter=12, angle_guard=2, rounding=round) won a similar bursty p99 spec (8 requests, p99 0.4us, err 2^-10) with est 813 luts+ffs. Here the burst is 4x larger (32) but the window is similar (0.44us), so m>=4 is likely needed; consider m=4..8, data_width 15-18, n_iter 12-15, angle_guard 1-2, rounding=round. Cost model underestimates LUTs ~19%, FFs ~11%, Fmax ~10% vs yosys+nextpnr-xilinx. unrolled_k never reached a front; iterative too slow for burst draining.

args.lesson: For 32-request-per-tick CORDIC specs (32 req/us, p99 batch <= 0.44us, err <= 2^-12, min LUTs+FFs), pipelined_m m=4, data_width=16, n_iter=14, angle_guard=2, frac_guard=2, rounding=round wins (est 1137 luts+ffs, 97.8 MSPS, simulated p99 0.378us). m=4 suffices even for 32-deep bursts at 1us ticks because throughput 97.8 MSPS >> 32 MSPS; the p99 window is dominated by pipeline drain, not throughput. No L3/L4 measurements recorded; L5 back_annotate returned no_measured_data.
